domain: global virological surveillance - respiratory-epidemic activity prediction (international organisation publisher)
prediction_question: For a WHO FluNet reporting country with a history of systematic weekly specimen reporting, will influenza test positivity in ISO week W+4 exceed a fixed activity threshold (proposed: 10% positive of specimens processed), given that country's weekly FluNet laboratory series (specimens processed, influenza A/B detections by subtype, non-influenza respiratory-virus detections) through ISO week W?
prediction_time: End of ISO week W (the Sunday that closes week W): every feature is derived from weekly laboratory counts published for weeks <= W; the target is week W+4's row, which is not yet observed. FluNet is updated weekly (measured: on 2026-10-20 the table already carries week-start 2026-10-19), so a monthly refresh of this task is honest.
target_definition: Binary, computed from the source row of week W+4: influenza positivity = INF_ALL / (INF_ALL + INF_NEGATIVE) exceeds 0.10, with a minimum denominator of 50 specimens in the week. Unit: proportion of specimens testing positive for influenza. Reference frame: country x ISO week, SENTINEL and NONSENTINEL origin streams summed (the table's grain is country x ISO week x ORIGIN_SOURCE). Label source columns INF_ALL and INF_NEGATIVE are recorded in label_source_columns and must be absent from the shipped feature columns; the threshold and lead are to be pinned at construction against a named known-event fixture before any number is quoted.

construction_script: candidates/who-flunet-activity-exceedance/source/build.py (stdlib only, runs on a worker; --smoke + --source-url for bounded exercises)
split_strategy: Temporal, one row per country-week: train ISO years <=2019, eval 2020-2022, holdout 2023 onward. Measured on the full table (country-week grain, origin streams summed, denominator >= 50): train window 2005-2019 has 14,870 usable country-weeks; eval window 2020-2022 has 8,559 usable country-weeks of which 29.0% are positives (2,485) - the COVID-era base-rate break is a property of the phenomenon and is documented, not smoothed away; holdout window 2023 has 4,677 country-weeks (42.4% positive, 1,984), extending through 2024-2026 (12,707 country-weeks, 48.3% positive, 6,135). Positives cluster by country-season: 278 clustered country-years in the eval window, 400 in 2024-2026. Construction must restrict to country-weeks where negatives are systematically reported (see measurements: pre-2015 rows are ~uniform-positive where negatives are missing, so those rows cannot carry the rate frame), and the clustered count, not the row count, is the effective sample-size figure.

measurements.full_download_2026_10_20: GET https://xmart-api-public.who.int/FLUMART/VIW_FNT?$format=csv -> HTTP 200, 30.8 MiB, 189,645 rows, 4.0 s, single request (coordinator). Table spans ISO years 1995-2026; latest week-start present: 2026-10-19 (i.e. updated to the current week).
measurements.grain_2026_10_20: Grain is country x ISO week x ORIGIN_SOURCE (SENTINEL 59,391 rows / NONSENTINEL 43,366 / NOTDEFINED 86,888). 148,355 distinct country-week keys over 189 countries/territories; France 2025 example: 104 rows over 52 weeks = two origin streams. Aggregation for the task grain must sum or select streams explicitly.
measurements.split_window_counts_2026_10_20: Computed from the downloaded table at country-week grain (streams summed, denominator INF_ALL+INF_NEGATIVE >= 50): 2005-2019: 14,870 country-weeks, 81.8% positive - INFLATED, see negatives trap; 2020-2022: 8,559 country-weeks, 2,485 positive (29.0%); 2023: 4,677 country-weeks, 1,984 positive (42.4%); 2024-2026: 12,707 country-weeks, 6,135 positive (48.3%). Clustered positives (country-years with >=1 positive week): 278 (eval window), 131 (2023), 400 (2024-2026).
measurements.negatives_frame_trap_2026_10_20: Pre-2015 FluNet rows mostly lack INF_NEGATIVE, so positivity computed as INF_ALL/(INF_ALL+INF_NEGATIVE) is 100% by construction there: the 1995-2004 window measures 931/931 country-weeks positive (a uniform result - the reference-frame red flag, not a finding). The construction must restrict to weeks where negatives are systematically reported (or pin the frame with a known-event fixture) and cross-check aggregate positivity curves against the publisher's own chart app (https://worldhealthorg.shinyapps.io/flunetchart/, linked from the FluNet page).
measurements.sample_probe_2026_10_20: $filter=ISO2 eq 'FR': 1,693 rows, ISO_YEAR 1997-2026, week-start range through 2026-10-05; recent French off-season weeks: INF_ALL 4-7 against SPEC_PROCESSED_NB 126-169 (positivity ~3-5%), illustrating both classes around a 10% threshold.
measurements.per_year_volume_2026_10_20: $filter=ISO_YEAR eq 2026 -> 1,476 KiB, 9,226 rows, 1.3 s; ISO_YEAR eq 2010 -> 926 KiB, 5,276 rows, 0.8 s; the GHO OData API (ghoapi.azureedge.net) was also probed for comparison: 3,099 indicators, anonymous; its annual panels were set aside (cholera indicator CHOLERA_0000000001 ends 2016 - stale; see notes).
measurements.construction_smoke_2026_10_20: Bounded local exercise of source/build.py before the worker launch: $filter=(ISO_YEAR eq 2024) or (ISO_YEAR eq 2025) -> 4,171,091 bytes in one request (0.6 s on re-fetch), eligible-row pipeline, timing self-check 200 rows recomputed against a series physically truncated at week W: 0 mismatches; 0 duplicate row_ids; 2,000-row holdout-only sample at 36.8% positive, 54 clustered country-years. Smoke mode skips split-capacity, fixture-coverage and trap assertions that a two-year window cannot carry.
measurements.france_fixture_pinned_2026_10_20: The record's proposed fixture ('France 2024-25 peak positivity must exceed 40%') was a candidate figure, and construction measured it wrong for this frame: blended positivity (ORIGIN_SOURCE streams summed, denominator INF_ALL+INF_NEGATIVE) peaks at 0.2379 in the week of 2025-01-27 over the 2024-W40..2025-W15 season (28 measurable weeks), and July-August 2024/2025 off-season weeks max at 0.0071. The 40% figure belongs to sentinel-only curves of stronger seasons, not to the blended frame. Pinned fixture: season peak in (0.15, 0.95] and off-season max < 0.10 - which pins threshold 0.10 and lead 4 weeks with measured margin on both sides. Asserted at build from the source; smoke run measured it on the 2024+2025 slice.

measurements.trap_acceptance_flunet_002: Measured on the full table: the 1995-2004 window holds 931 pre-rule country-weeks at 100% positive - byte-for-byte the discovery session's 931/931 measurement, reproduced independently - and the systematic-negative rule leaves 14 of them. review_response_2026_10_21.question: Is the reported 0.8700 eval AUC more than seasonal predictability, and does it beat a one-line rule?
review_response_2026_10_21.rows: the released artifact, private release v2026.10 (5 assets, 6,576,498 B); public-train 5,779 rows / public-eval 6,831 rows

persistence_week_W_positivity.note: reproduced independently from the released rows; score is week-W positivity, known at the prediction instant

independent_calendar_only_gbm.note: external replication, country one-hot + cyclical week + hierarchical seasonal prior; per-year 2020 0.6561, 2021 0.6263, 2022 0.5919, 2023 0.6534

review_response_2026_10_21.conclusion: Not seasonal predictability: calendar-only tops out at 0.6269 while the full model reaches 0.8700. But the full model is BELOW week-W persistence (0.8929), so the current baseline demonstrates no value over a one-line rule. On this construction the label is essentially persistent, not a forecast of change.

prevalence_shift.note: train targets 2005-2020 (concentrated 2015-2019), eval 2020-2023, holdout 2023-2026; the eval window is the COVID disruption, so this is an out-of-distribution test as much as a temporal one.

sentinel_only_feasibility.source: WHO FluNet full table, xmart-api-public.who.int/FLUMART/VIW_FNT (189,649 rows)
sentinel_only_feasibility.note: sentinel-only is feasible but shrinks the eligible panel by about 3x in the eval window; 46% of source rows carry ORIGIN_SOURCE=NOTDEFINED, so the current combined positivity mixes three categories.

review_response_2026_10_21.lag_audit: not performed: the publisher exposes only the current vintage, so historical publication times and revisions are unavailable; a defensible cutoff must be assumed (W-1 or W-2) and stated.

prior_art: Kaggle mirror patricklford/flunet-global-influenza-programme-who (raw data only); arXiv 2505.10213 (LLM time-series experiment, no benchmark release); CDC FluSight (US ILINet challenge); ECDC Flusion (EU)
novelty_check.theirs: WHO publishes the FluNet surveillance data itself (weekly, anonymous CSV API) and Kaggle mirrors it raw (patricklford/flunet-global-influenza-programme-who, no task). arXiv 2505.10213 runs an LLM forecasting experiment on two univariate FluNet series (MAE/MAPE, no released task). CDC FluSight and ECDC Flusion are forecasting challenges on other sources (US ILINet, EU hospitalisations), not FluNet positivity.
novelty_check.ours: A binary country-week exceedance task on WHO FluNet laboratory positivity (INF_ALL/(INF_ALL+INF_NEGATIVE) > threshold at a 4-week lead), with disjoint temporal splits, a known-event fixture, systematic-negative-reporting gating rules, and a scored contract for coding-agent evaluation. No ML-ready version of this task exists: the formulation, threshold/lead, splits, gating and validation are the contribution.
novelty_check.rule: A dataset that already exists in ML-ready form is not published. Mirroring is a failure mode, not a contribution.

baseline.note: Measured on the bytes being released (fetched, digest-verified), not a rebuild. The XGBoost pass (0.8700) sits below the persistence reference (0.8929 eval), which is recorded as measured headroom information.
